narrative:
The model estimates a 74% chance that you will leave your current job. Based on patterns from many similar employees, this leads to your promotion being denied, as the organization wants to invest in people more likely to stay long-term.

The decision is driven primarily by three key aspects of your background. First, your total years of experience across all jobs (6-10 years) was the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward leaving. Employees with this mid-level experience are more likely to move on than those with very short careers. Second, the time you have spent in your current role (1-5 years) also strongly pointed toward departure. This is shorter than the tenure of many who stay, suggesting you may still be exploring options. Finally, not having received other job offers while at this company worked in the opposite direction, mildly encouraging the model to predict you would stay.

Taken together, your experience profile signals higher mobility risk. The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you openly. You might reflect on whether additional responsibilities, better recognition, or clearer growth paths could increase your commitment. Addressing these areas could improve both your satisfaction and future promotion prospects. (218 words)
